overall_justification: V3 is the first cut whose story reads end to end without the picture contradicting it: one finish, one clock, a visible set-down, an oblivious exit, yelling that reads as yelling. It is held at 7 because the peaks now break in sound and acting: the triumph plays twice, there are digital-zero dropouts mid-climax and a wrap-glitch on the final card, sad lines are spoken through a grin, S054b has a third arm, and the S095 crossing never reads.
trend: 4.0 -> 6.0 -> 7.0. Every auditor went up again, but the gains are halving (+2.1 mean, then +0.7). V2 predicted 7.5 and V3 came in at 7.0. The missing half point comes from fixes that were half-applied (G15 arena haze/bloom, G16 warm sources, G12 gestures, G08 S065) and from fixes that were never checked against the render and caused new faults: the G10 min-water-fill clamps every short shot back to 2.2 s, G52 was marked done but L043 still doesn't cut in, and the new music stops leave digital-zero holes. V4 rule: an item is done only after it has been checked on the rendered stills and the audio scan.
verdict: V3 tells the story. A stranger can follow the hook, the rule, the escalation, the friendship break, the plant and the payoff without a single contradiction in the climax. The workshop turn (S066-S069) and the B35 action cut are reference-grade. What holds it back is no longer logic but polish at the exact moments that matter most. (1) Sound at the peaks: triumph_resolve plays on S091b at 0:05 and then again from bar 1 on the horn, S088 is 1.95 s of digital zero in the middle of the climax, and the final title card ends on an ending_light wrap burst. (2) The two payoff images: S095's wheel is on the checker from frame 1 and creeps ~1 s ahead of the horn, unlit, and S091b is still a rounded UI card. (3) Acting: the generic talk mouth is a smile, so Noah's hurt line (S064) and Eli's apology (S100) are delivered grinning. S054b shows a third arm. S102 ends on a frozen mid-stride. (4) Craft ceilings: the arena (a third of the runtime) measures the same as V2, the warm payoff is a brown wash, and the rhythm went more metronomic (CV 0.42, 23 shots at exactly 2.20 s) because of a default in timeline.js. All P0s are small and local. No script change except the optional L077 pickup.
publishable_note: Not as-is. It can be followed, but the S109 audio glitch on the final card, the 2 s dropout in S088, the double triumph and the S054b third arm look and sound broken to a first-time YouTube viewer, and the two emotional lines read as smiling. Every P0 is a one-shot or one-function change (roughly a day). After P0 alone V3 is publishable at about 7.5. After P0+P1 it is a confident upload.

conflicts_resolved.topic: Music from the switch to 0:01: story offers no bed (sfx riser) or a tension tail; logic offers a tension sting.
conflicts_resolved.decision: Delete both the B35 beat stop and the S091b triumph, so the tension_competition already restarted on S089 runs on until the existing S094b stop. Add a riser sfx for lift.
conflicts_resolved.why: The root cause is the B35 {stop,at:.15} that leaves 1.3 s of nothing and then the early triumph. The cue is 60 s and has only played 10 s by S094b, so there's no fade risk. One tension line from 'What do I do?!' to 0:01, then silence, heartbeat and triumph on the horn, gives the cleanest release.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S092: cut it (story: unreadable in 1.1 s, stalls the run) vs keep it (rhythm calls B35 reference-grade with it, logic counts it in the causal chain).
conflicts_resolved.decision: Keep it at 1.1 s and simplify it to one wordless image (H20).
conflicts_resolved.why: The whole moral depends on the viewer understanding why the backup works, and L068 'Missed the barrier' lands on it. The problem is legibility, not existence. A trace that dies against a trace that survives reads in one glance. Revisit cutting it only if V4 viewers still can't read it.

conflicts_resolved.topic: Flash grammar in B35 and the flashback: animation says drop the white tin on S091b, story says drop it on S094b and S095, rhythm and lighting want it added on S091 and S088. The rubric requires shots under 1.2 s to be deliberate flash or impact cuts.
conflicts_resolved.decision: White flashes only for entering and leaving memory (S087 in, S088 out). In B35 the only light bursts are emitted in-world: the blue LED ignite (S091b) and the warm horn flash (S095 at 1.2). S091b, S094b and S079c are marked impact:true, which satisfies the rubric's impact-cut exception. S091 stays a plain 1.2 s cut.
conflicts_resolved.why: Four white flashes in 7 s read as camera flashes and blunt the two that matter. Motivated light bursts carry the same punch and tell the story.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S091b staging: logic wants a crop of the real PR.robot, lighting wants to relight the current chassis, story notes 'left side' is only a caption.
conflicts_resolved.decision: Logic's crop of the real robot's rear-left corner and wheel, with lighting's housing and spill values and animation's sputter ignite (H05).
conflicts_resolved.why: Only the real robot geometry links the shot to S060 and gives 'left' a place. The lighting values then make the LED, not the box, the brightest thing.

conflicts_resolved.topic: Runtime: rhythm adds long takes (S070 3 s, S102 3.6 s, S035 hold, S103 5 s, S085b, S073b, S079b/c) and also shortens punch cuts; logic would restore L076 (~6 s).
conflicts_resolved.decision: Do the rhythm reshaping, don't restore L076, and keep the hard 330-360 s build guard. If V4 goes over 360, drop the optional S035 extension first, then trim S103 back to 4 s.
conflicts_resolved.why: The goal is variance (CV), not length. The floor change saves ~8-10 s across the 2.2 s clamped shots, roughly paying for the new long takes and splits. L076 restates the premise the rule card already shows.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S066: animation wants Noah's hand to withdraw, while story and rhythm praise the stillness of the hold.
conflicts_resolved.decision: Withdraw the hand after the click (3.4-4.2 s, slow inOut), keep still:true on the body, and scale the tool up to .9.
conflicts_resolved.why: The hold stays still and silent. The only movement is the hand leaving the tool, which is the meaning of the beat ('he leaves it behind').

conflicts_resolved.topic: S061 (rhythm likes the warm/cool alternation by speaker) vs logic (Eli must be back-turned and not looking up in both S061 and S065).
conflicts_resolved.decision: Compatible: keep the reverse plate and its cool light, and change only Eli's blocking (back-turned, typing, laptop facing him) and Noah's FG side (H11).
conflicts_resolved.why: The angle is right. The acting on it contradicts the script.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S102: rhythm wants a low wide at a different scale, animation and logic need a readable contact bump and laugh.
conflicts_resolved.decision: Both: a low wide with heads in the upper third at a size where the bump and laugh read (h >= 560), plus FG crowd in the bottom 25%.
conflicts_resolved.why: The low angle makes the last arena image different from S099, and the contact and laugh give it an action. Neither works without the other.

conflicts_resolved.topic: V2 G52 marked done (L043 interruption) vs the story auditor measuring +0.22 s in the render.
conflicts_resolved.decision: The story auditor is right. The showrunner traced it to timeline.js semantics: gap is the pause after a line, so it was set on the wrong line (H10).
conflicts_resolved.why: Verified in source: timeline.js line 21 lastGap = o.gap applies after the line. The timeline JSON shows L042 end 192.12 and L043 start 192.34.

showrunner_findings: B35 music root cause: the beat-level {stop,at:.15} (act3.js:201) plus the S091b triumph cue (act3.js:204) create both the 1.3 s hole and the double triumph.
mix.py:70 wraps any music segment modulo the track length. That is the S109 ending_light burst, and it can recur wherever a cue outlasts its file.
timeline.js:21: gap applies after a line, so G52's gap on L043 never interrupted L042.

predicted_v4_rationale: If P0+P1 are done and verified on render: story_flow 8.3 (the peaks sound intentional, the payoff images read, the ending keeps its piano), logic_sense 8.0 (no visible nonsense left, only P2 staging nits), shot_rhythm 7.8 (CV ~.6, real punch cuts, hall and overhead variety, still short of the reference's long-take share), lighting 8.0 (an arena with real highlights, an emitted gold payoff, a lit hero ECU, no rim ghosts), animation 7.0 (mouths match feelings, the key beats are acted, bodies still mostly lib-driven).
